name: Daniel

objectives.text: Retell how Daniel kept praying to God and how God shut the lions' mouths to protect him
Name Shadrach, Meshach, and Abednego and recall that they would not bow down to the king's golden statue
Recall from Daniel that God rules over all kings and kingdoms
Describe how Daniel and his friends refused the king's food and how God blessed them with health and wisdom
Summarize the story of the fiery furnace, including the fourth figure in the fire and the king's response
Retell the story of the writing on the wall and explain what the words meant for King Belshazzar
Explain Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the statue made of metals, including the four kingdoms and the stone that becomes God's everlasting kingdom
Describe the historical setting of Daniel, including the exile of Judah to Babylon and Daniel's service under Babylonian and Persian kings
Compare the pride and humbling of Nebuchadnezzar with Daniel's humility in giving credit to God
Explain how Daniel and his friends served faithfully in a pagan government while refusing to compromise their worship of God
Identify the structure of Daniel as court narratives followed by visions and note the shift between Hebrew and Aramaic
Analyze how the theme of God's sovereignty over the nations is developed across the narratives of Daniel
Interpret the vision of the four beasts and the Ancient of Days and compare it with the statue dream of chapter 2
Explain how Jesus identified himself with the Son of Man of Daniel 7 and how this reveals his kingship
Explain the main features of apocalyptic literature using examples from the visions of Daniel
Analyze Daniel's prayer of confession as a response to God's covenant promises spoken through Jeremiah
Interpret the vision of the ram and the goat using the angel's explanation and identify the historical kingdoms it describes
Construct a timeline of the seventy weeks prophecy that compares the traditional messianic reading with other major interpretations
Explain how Daniel 12 teaches the bodily resurrection and final judgment and connect it to the teaching of Jesus
Analyze the portrayal of heavenly conflict and the role of angels such as Michael in Daniel's final vision
Evaluate arguments for a sixth-century and a Maccabean dating of Daniel, including the role of assumptions about predictive prophecy
Trace how the book of Revelation draws on the imagery of Daniel's visions
Create a study on living faithfully as exiles that draws on Daniel and connects it to New Testament teaching for believers

changes: Kept and reworded real competencies (lions' den, three friends, God's rule, fiery furnace, writing on the wall, statue dream, pride vs humility, sovereignty, four beasts, Son of Man, apocalyptic genre, seventy weeks, dating, exile study). Replaced the affective 'apply courage' objective with an observable one on faithful service without compromise. Merged the dating and 'defend supernatural prediction' objectives into one evaluation. Added Daniel 1 food test, historical setting, book structure and languages, Daniel 9 prayer, ram and goat vision, resurrection in Daniel 12, heavenly conflict in Daniel 10, and Daniel's use in Revelation. Anchored objectives to verse ranges and added confessional references only where they state the doctrine taught.
